narrative_events.details: Seventh-year daily rites, lion and four weapons/ascetic ornaments; playful cosmic roar delights parents.

King receives hospitality and requests purohita for son’s wedding; Cāturmāsya prevents Kaśyapa travelling. Son substituted, bows parents, boards chariot; Aditi requires constant care and safe return, king agrees.
Narrative flashback identifies paternal uncle/brother,10000-year inverted smoky Sun tapas, weapon and dominion request. Sun sends unfailing radiant weapon; dominion not explicitly granted.
Child flies, intercepts weapon and tosses to test power; fall splits Dhūmrākṣa, fragments crush surrounding rocks/trees500bow-lengths. King wonders at destiny.
Sons accuse king of killing their father/protector. Afraid of Narāntaka king asserts wedding purpose and offers child. Child protests breach of parental trust and warns Kaśyapa’s anger.
Roar/breath launches attacking sons; after two muhūrtas they fall into Narāntaka city crushing homes. Messengers discover both alive and transmit their report.
1000rākṣasas ordered to capture child/kill if fighting. Roar kills some; others injured, including arrow-torn bellies, flee and report.
Survivors warn child unbeatable; Narāntaka ridicules warning, equips host and orders plunder/distraction or killing king and child. Commander threatens any disobedient demon.
City reception and sixteen-offering worship; eager women seek sight, one barred woman dies while meditating. Four social groups perceive varied forms according to disposition.
Child knowingly counters malicious play-embrace by crushing both demons; ten-yojana corpses and divine flower/praise follow.
Whirlwinds devastate city and lift chariot; child immobilizes chariot, grabs topknots, whirls and kills both. King bows recognizing divine creator and countless forms.
Axe splits disguised stone100ways; child fists emerging terrifying demon down after onlookers flee.
King seats, worships, feeds child/friends and prepares night bed after sandhyā; four guards stationed while king/queen retire by child’s leave.
After morning rites child plays. Kaśyapa’s friend Dharmadatta invites incarnate Lord to purify household; child willingly follows.
Two sent demons fall toward child as fighting donkeys; child grabs feet, whirls/smashes both dead. Direct sight confirms fame for Dharmadatta.
Rampaging disguised elephant fights royal animals amid destruction. Child refuses shelter, mounts and goads temples to death; falling body crushes homes. Rescued from corpse, carried indoors.
Devotee worships/feeds and gives Siddhi/Buddhi as dakṣiṇā, praises divine visit lifting ancestry; child seats/honors him and appears with both.
Dhūmrākṣa’s wife feigns kindly massage, applies poison, causes burning. Child knows evil, strikes head with coconut, exposing two-yojana corpse.
Renewed meal/worship and divine celebrations; king brings child home in musical procession. Lion/weapon appearance and paired attendants celebrated; hearing benefit concludes.

King recounts victories with retrospective names Kūṭa/Kuṇḍa and proposes wedding preparations. Two ministers blame continued child presence for dangers; wedding postponed fortnight/month with agreement.
Revenge trio plans fire, wind and devouring. Vast tiger-maw and mouth-fire destroy city; refugees swallowed, mistaking mouth for cave. Source fire attribution retained with textual caution.

King protects entrusted child while abandoning belongings/family, regrets but recalls duty and earlier rescues. Fort/water defense fails against wind-fire; armies/citizens flee, king/child lose and search one another.

Child enters closed tiger-maw, expands/splits demon dead. One half cast away, other playhouse; captives arise. Drinks fire, footstroke crushes final attackers (Vidāraṇa wording), yogamāyā revives all dead/restores city.
People/king praise rescue and resurrection. Healthy homecomings/daily rites, gifts/peace-worship/redistribution and rest conclude; devotional hearing yields desires/no disasters.

King’s meal invitation reveals child already fed/adorned by remote bright-fourth worship. Child identifies sage, ascetic trunk/ressemblance, temporal knowledge and cosmic power; three deities seek sight.
Vināyaka dictates first invitation/name. King travels armed horseback, honors sage/hermitage, gives wedding invitation; identifies Sun-lineage self and Kaśyapa’s child.
Sage asks deity form; king describes divine four-arm birth then ordinary seventh-year Brahmacārin. Sage refuses since not own meditation-deity, while offering obedience if own Lord calls.
King accepts cannot compel. Sage compassionately hand-blesses and returns closed-eyed king instantly home; king reports happiness/sorrow and warns coercing brāhmaṇas brings ashes.
After exact report child laughs, supplies name Gajānana and instantly sends king back. Sage ecstatic on name, sets out; Earth trembles, reassured, and third step reaches Kāśī.

Sage threatens curse, refuses two-arm child as lesser. Describes own ten-arm peacock form; child adopts exact lotus-seated form. Sage loves/dances/worships, Lord embraces ten-armed, king worships both.
Lord explains forms responsive to devotion and earth/Brahmā/Aditi incarnation cause; promises demon destruction, god restoration and departure after brothers killed, as future purpose.
Sage requests repeated direct sight of exact form and Āśāpūraka name’s fame. Lord grants both and adds all wishes fulfilled/constant remembrance. Child plays; sage meditates.
Witnesses marvel, king praises rare sight, feeds/beds child and retires with permission.
